Paragraph 8, "in conformity with its international obligations, Croatia reiterates the inviolability of United Nations premises and establishments and its vehicles and all those therein," and I'm reading this out fully because it becomes relevant, "and thus commits all Croatian authorities to fully respect such inviolability." That, again, was one of the terms that had been established between the UN and the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That was concluded on the 6th of August and you arrived in Knin on the 7th?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You arrived with Mr. Akashi?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he was the special representative for the Secretary General?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And his visit to the UNCRO compound on the 7th was part of a large delegation of UN officials who came to see the circumstances of the camp on that day?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Well not only of the camp, of course, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Camp and Knin and whatever else they could see?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Particularly, the camp was a focus because of the large numbers of people who'd gone to the camp during the previous days of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you part of the tour that Mr. Akashi had when he went to the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not participate in the meetings he held with Croatian authorities at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, may I invite you to find a suitable moment within the next one or two moments to conclude for the day so that we can spend some time on the MFIs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I will ask one more question. I won't introduce a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were not at the meetings, what were you doing in the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: On that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: I have difficulty recalling. Of course, it's been almost 13 years. But I suppose that I met or spoke with other UN officials about what they had seen in the previous days, I inquired as to the circumstances of the displaced persons, how they came to be inside the camp confines, and also we had to deal with basic matters like accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And those are all issues which are relevant to the Akashi/Saranac agreement of the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we stop there. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Flynn, we have to deal with a few practical matters, but you don't have to stay for that. I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone, whomever it is, about your testimony, whether already given or whether still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I ask the court a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if I could have a hard copy of the Akashi/Saranac agreement because I don't actually have it in my papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any problem by any of the parties that the witness looks at it overnight?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the parties, they'll provide you through the Victims and Witness Section with a copy. If it's here at this moment to be given to the witness, we could right away; but if not, the parties are invited to deal with that immediately after the session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you are excused. Could you please follow the usher. I see that there is a copy already available. So if Mr. Usher if you would take that from Mr. Kay and give it to Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to deal with the exhibits. You have received a list; nevertheless, I'll start with two items which are not on the list, that's D13 and D14. These are the comparative videos which have been meanwhile uploaded in e-court, as I understand. The first one mainly about the sirens and breaking of glass, and the second one about what was in the facility of the impact of what appeared to be shell impact. Was it a park area or was it a police station? It has been uploaded. I would first like to ask whether there's any objection against.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe there is, but unfortunately that wasn't on my list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do understand. Okay. The Prosecution will tell us not later than by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, that's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then, of course, the whole issue apparently seems to be manipulation of video. Mr. Misetic, anything else on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to go through the list in five minutes. Then D10, any objection, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I spoke with Mr. Cayley about that document. I understand that is no longer being tendered by the Cermak Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then D10 will be vacated. D11 is still without a translation, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my understanding now that we have uploaded the proper version, and we seek leave of the Trial Chamber to replace the version that was in e-court yesterday with this new version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We had an incomplete version yesterday. That has been repaired. Do I understand that the translation is there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you seen the translation, Mr. Tieger, or would you reserve -- would you need sometime to check whether this letter by Witness 6 is -- you will remember the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I am hesitant because I don't want to delay the process. But if the Court gives the opportunity to do so, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You get one day to make sure your translation issue is off the table. The other matter has been repaired. We would like to hear from you tomorrow, and even you could perhaps in the beginning of the court session say no objection to this, no objection, then I can immediately deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think that will be efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we go on, D D12, any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D12 is admitted into evidence. D16, aerial image, any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I spoke with Mr. Misetic about this, Your Honour. I think the -- I think, other than the description of the exhibit, which is erroneous --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It changes already. It should say Zastava Film not Veritas Film crew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Veritas being replaced by Zastava, any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D16 then with new description is now admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think I should have made that clearer. I thought that we addressed that. It's not just the nature of the crew that was there, but my recollection is that in the course of testimony, the Court pointed out it wasn't -- that what the document indicated was not precisely where they were located, but the angle of which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, on the document it says where it was located. But on the basis of evidence, I have great difficulty to accept that on what the witness said, that he could confirm that these were the locations. Whether they were or not, I'm not aware of. That's just a claim at this moment. I take it that you accept that these were the directions from which the video was made. Although you do not object admission into evidence for practical purposes, this does not imply that you accept the precise locations as the locations from which it was filmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's my understanding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Then we move on to D17.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I looked at the transcript as quickly as I could to try to refresh my own recollection of the tendering and discussion about that document. I understood from the transcript that was withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's not my understanding from the transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think, well, we'll have to look at it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please deal with it. D17 we'll hear from tomorrow by both parties. D18.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a slightly different problem. Again, the problem is not with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Mrksic issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's one aspect of it. The other aspect is that the descriptions on the document itself were not necessarily confirmed by the witness, and I'm concerned that this gives rise to later confusion where the document is presented, it has a characterisation, the witness doesn't affirm that or does so only in part. Then the exhibit as labelled appears to give rise to different evidence than was provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest the following to the parties: It's well understood that descriptions are not always accepted by the other party; nevertheless, these are descriptions that were presented to the witness. But at the same time, I'd like to invite the parties that if you want to point out something, that you make it A or B or whatever, so that the witness then can tell us what it is or say that the lines drawn there are not correctly drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's been a problem for a few exhibits that we can keep track of and be aware of the distinction between what the witness said and what the document indicates, but over time I think it could become a significant problem when the parties and the court later try to determine what the evidence actually is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, since the witness was not, I think, asked about the descriptions as such, but was invited to tell what he saw, could it be a practical solution that D17 -- the same would be true I think for D18 -- no, not for D18 - for D17 that a new version will be produced without the text on it because that's the picture of which the witness was invited to look, then it would be now on the record that he looked at a picture including some text, but that we then removed that text in order to avoid confusion for the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would be happy to do that, Your Honour. My only concern is my recollection that the witness made three markings on the exhibit. He identified, I believe, the army hall, the RSK headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we then could do is try to have a colour copy made of it and then redacted the text, and then to submit the marked copy but then without the text as replacing D17. Would that be agreeable to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour, except I think you are, indeed, talking about D18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think I'm talking about D17 -- no. You're right. It's D18. It's the four black and white pictures showing houses located 20 metres from, and should it be Mrksic headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It is RSK headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: RSK headquarters. So then we get a new version of D18, and it's now on the record. It's not exactly anymore what has been shown to the witness, although the picture and the markings are the same. D23, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D23 is admitted into evidence. D24 --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. We have a problem there. D24, we have no translations yet, so I should have not admitted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have no translation as well, but we have assurances that we will be in possession of the original version of the document for the beginning of next week. Therefore, the translation will be much more appropriate because it will be completely legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then we leave D23 and D24 on our MFI list. D25.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, my only opportunity to see that was in e-court. It appears the last three pages of the document are still in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still in B/C/S. So you would like to come back to that. D25 is still MFIed, no position taken yet. D26, any position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not with respect to D26 and D27, but they should both be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, D26 and 27, yes, it's already indicated on the list confidential. Admitted into evidence, under seal. P17, any objections? That is the map. Is it uploaded? I do understand it was, meanwhile. No objections. Then P17 is admitted into evidence. P18. That is the full long video showing, as we understand, Knin in those early days of August, but without a transcript and without the voiceover being in evidence just the pictures. Objection? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. And I think that if I understand the agreement correctly, because one of the participants in that process is not here, Mr. Misetic will correct me if I am wrong, but that -- I think that should be admitted along with 65 ter number 3759, which is the -- what has been referred to as the raw footage of the same -- well, the raw footage from which P18 was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The complete raw footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm, at this point, not sure now if 65 ter 5739 and P18 are one and the same or not. Is P18 the Veritas?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's my understanding and that's why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In any event, the raw footage. That would then be tendered from the bar table, I take it, because the raw footage was not shown to the witness; and, therefore, we'll then hear, Mr. Tieger, if you would then come back to this issue once we have reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have no objection to the raw footage coming in, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if you indicate to Mr. Registrar what the footage will be, then he'll assign a new number to it, and then we can decide on a mission towards the admission of the raw footage. Therefore, P18, any further objections? That's the redacted or at least the version of the video. Then P18 is admitted into evidence. Perhaps unnecessary to say, but P17, of course, was already indicated on the list as being confidential. So P17 should be under seal. Well, that at least shortens our list a bit. Mr. Mikulicic, unless there is some great urgency, I'm already stealing time from my colleagues who might need this courtroom this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will take only five seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will turn back to the document D23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think I mistakenly stated we have no translation. We have translation for that document but we don't have translation for D24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Tieger, have you had an opportunity already to already look at D23, that's the letter from the Republican Committee Of Education, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought I indicated no objection to D23, and then the concern about the problem related to the translation for D24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then D23 is also admitted into evidence. We have shortened our list, although it's not completely gone yet. We'll adjourn. Apologies for the Chamber that use this courtroom, and we request of Mr. Registrar to inform them that we left the courtroom nine minutes late. We adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00 same courtroom.
